bottom_line: In IMPROVE-IT, simvastatin–ezetimibe vs simvastatin monotherapy reduced the primary composite end point (hazard ratio, 0.936; 95% confidence interval, 0.89 to 0.99).
implications: These data support that, in patients after acute coronary syndrome, adding ezetimibe to simvastatin (vs simvastatin alone) was associated with a lower 7-year Kaplan–Meier rate of the primary composite end point (32.7% vs 34.7%) with hazard ratio 0.936 (95% CI, 0.89 to 0.99). The reported estimates also show similar 7-year Kaplan–Meier cardiovascular death (6.9% vs 6.8) and all-cause death (15.4% vs 15.3) between groups, and similar prespecified safety end points in Table 3.
